 Peixoto | 'It's about finding the right players for the game'
 21st November 2026 
 Cesar Peixoto has welcomed the return to fitness of several of his Wolves squad ahead of Saturday’s Championship clash with Charlton Athletic at Molineux.
 Jordan James, Bertrand Traore and Boubacar Traore have all returned to training during the international break after a spell on the sidelines, while Fer Lopez and Jean-Ricner Bellegarde pulled out from representing their countries to recover from minor knocks.
 With more players at his disposal heading into the weekend’s game, Peixoto has explained why he is prepared to continue rotating his side as he looks to get his team through another busy slate of second tier fixtures.
 On the latest injury news 
 “Jordan is better, not 100%. He was training with us yesterday and today but he’s a player who isn’t 100% and we’re going to manage with him, but he’s started training with us.
 “Bertrand and Bouba are better also. They’ve been training with since last week, but they still need time to stay with the right fitness and the right rhythm of the game, but they’re now going to be an option to play with the team because they’re not injured now.
 “This has been a shorter international break, which is better for us because we’ve had more players available to train with the team, but in the first week, Fer wasn’t training because he was recovering from his injury. Bellegarde only started training yesterday and today, and he’s still not 100 per cent, but Fer did a good week of training.”
 On Lopez’s fitness 
 “I think he’s in a better condition. He’s not 100 per cent, but he’s been able to train during the week, which is important.
 “During the last international break, he came back carrying an injury and he was playing through pain and not training properly. It was difficult to manage because he was playing, recovering and then playing again.
 “He’s an important player for us, so we have to manage his minutes carefully, but I think he’ll be in a better condition for this game than he was previously.”
 On getting his internationals back up to speed 
 “It’s always difficult, not only because of the minutes they play, but also because of the travel. Sometimes they travel for a lot of hours and when they arrive, they tell the staff they’re tired because they haven’t slept properly on the plane. It’s difficult for them, but we have to try to recover them as soon as possible and prepare them for the game.
 “We have players who have played a lot of minutes and travelled a lot of hours, so we have to manage those situations. The good news is that we haven’t had any injuries from the international break, which is important for us.
 “It’s important that we manage the training properly because the players need these sessions with the team. We normally play, recover, play and recover, so having this period to work with some of the players has been beneficial.”
 #WOLCHA 
 On managing the squad for the Championship 
 “I always focus on the next game and I always put the best players in the team to try to win that game. We analyse the opposition and, in some situations, we make changes based on what we see.
 “Against Wrexham, for example, we analysed their set-pieces and crosses, which are very dangerous, so we made a change and brought Toti into the team to help us control those situations. Unfortunately, we conceded from a cross, but overall, we controlled those moments well.
 “It’s not only about managing minutes, but also about finding the right players for the game. I look at the match over 90 minutes, not just the starting 11. We have to consider what might happen during the game and whether we have solutions from the bench.
 “We want to put together a competitive team and competitive players to try to win every game. We also look at how players feel, how they’ve recovered and whether there is a risk of injury if they play too many games. I look game after game. I don’t select a starting 11 today because I’m thinking about the next three games – I select the best team for this game.”
 On finding his best starting 11 
 “If you look before Wrexham, we had three or four games where we played a similar starting 11. I don’t like to change the team all the time and I don’t manage minutes just for the sake of changing the team. I look at the work during the week, the players who are in the best condition and what I believe is the best starting 11 to play in our way and win the game.
 “Sometimes we have to make changes because of injuries, fatigue, travel or the number of games we’re playing. We have players who go away with their national teams, and some travel a long way and play a lot of minutes, so we have to be clever in managing those situations.
 “With players like Trippier or Raul, because of their age, we sometimes have to manage things differently. They’re important players for us, and we want them available, but we have to find the best way to manage their minutes and keep them in the best condition to help the team.
 “We have a lot of games in the Championship, sometimes six games in two weeks, and if we play the same players too many minutes all the time, there could be a drop in their level towards the end of the season, so we also have to manage that carefully.
 “We know our best 11, we know the best team we want to play, but circumstances can change. I don’t like making changes all the time, but sometimes I have to change because of the injuries, the tiredness and the travels of the international break.”
